steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Place bananas into a large resealable plastic bag; seal the bag and smoosh bananas with your fingers until well mashed. Set aside.

Mix together brown sugar and butter in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy, 1 to 2 minutes. Cut a corner from the plastic bag; squeeze mashed bananas into brown sugar mixture in the bowl. Add egg, milk, cinnamon, and vanilla; beat on medium speed until well combined. Mix in flour, baking powder, baking soda, and kosher salt on low speed just until smooth, about 1 minute. Spread into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned on top and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Brown Sugar Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: This brown sugar banana bread is super soft, moist, and packed with rich, deep flavor thanks to lots of ripe, sweet bananas, butter, and cinnamon.

review.reviewBody: Phenomenal banana bread recipe! Very flavorful, moist and full of great banana flavor. I only made a couple minor mods to the original recipe: I cut the butter down to 2 tbl., only used 1/2 c. brown sugar and substituted whole wheat four for the AP. With the flour switch, I was nervous that the texture would be 'off,' but I was wrong! It turned out super moist and perfect...and the sweetness from the 4 bananas more than made up for the brown sugar I cut out. Excellent recipe...will definitely make it again and again!

I did not have 4 bananas, so I used 2 bananas and 2 dessert cups of chunked pineapple and I drained the liquid. I put the batter into cupcake liners in a muffin pan. I filled the cups 3/4 full. I baked them at 350 for 30-40 min. It made 24 banana, pineapple cupcakes or muffins. They were moist and very tasty. I will make them again and add a little more cinnamon and ice them with a cream cheese icing. Very tasty and easy to make.

This made very yummy banana bread. It was especially good heated up. The bread was pretty dense and moist, but very delicious, and the crust was soft and sticky. I would say maybe add some more spices, and maybe even more cinnamon. I think nutmeg might be a good addition. Very yummy, and was popular with my friends. It's good to use overripe bananas, and also I did not do the plastic bag mashing method I just put them in the bowl with all the other stuff and mashed them in there with a fork, and it turned out fine. I didn't want to waste the plastic. This might only work if the bananas are really overripe though. I also do not have an electric mixer, but it worked perfectly fine by hand.

Great recipe & I have never been wowed by banana bread . Like another person I cut the sugar to 3/4 cup and added a half cup of mini chocolate chips. I didn't do that whole plastic bag thing with the bananas , just mashed them with a fork. Delicious

Loved it. Followed directions exactly, and had everything at room temp. Be sure to beat the sugar and butter well. I did sprinkle coarse sugar on top before baking. I don’t like wet banana bread, so as others suggested, I baked for 60 minutes. Then I turned the oven down to 300 and baked another 20. It was perfect, and I’ll make it again.

Made this for a women's brunch event and it was a huge hit. Ladies wanted the recipe. It's such nice change from my usual banana bread. Be sure to add the brown sugar on top before baking. It gives a little crunch.

My go to banana bread recipe! Taste amazing and it’s also very forgiving/versatile. Depending on how many bananas I have, I just go based on that (3-5 any size) and it comes out fine. I also add pinch of nutmeg and use dark brown sugar instead of light for a deeper flavour. I do find with my oven it may take longer than the required time though, so I make muffins instead for a shorter bake (17-20 min).

I did not smoosh the bananas in a bag. There is no need to do that. Just mash them into the bread mix. Also I added chocolate chips and I just used regular salt. Worked perfectly. My grandkids loved it!

This turned out to be a real hit in my house. I made it in muffin tins to be an easy on the go grab, and they went! The recipe yielded 2 dozen good sized muffins, I added a cup of chocolate chips and changed nothing otherwise. Cooked in under 30 mins

Of all of my banana bread recipes, THIS has become my absolute favorite! Family and friends all think it is the best banana bread they have ever tasted. I have remained true to the original recipe, but I have learned that if you add more than the specified 1½ cups of bananas, they will all sink down to the bottom of the loaf into a soggy blob! For an added treat, I occasionally add 1 cup of craisins to the flour mixture to coat them before I add them to the wet ingredients. Craisins, like raisins, go good with this recipe.

Great recipe, and I have tried oh so many banana bread recipes. I had ripe peaches as well as bananas, so I used two of each and it turned out great. I prefer a 9" square baking pan over a loaf pan. It solves the problem of dry edges and a mushy center. This recipe was easy and the brown sugar sends it over the top. You could probably use less sugar, but I think it's good as is. The family loved it and asked me to make more right away, so I've made it 3 times in two weeks.
Delicious and I also did the biscoff version!
So easy to follow and definitely a favorite of my kids and grandson! I often take this into work too for co-workers.

The only thing I added to this recipe was some brown sugar sprinkled on top which gave it an almost caramel flavor and a bit of crunch. It was fabulous, and everyone who tried it said it was amazing! This one of my top two favorite banana bread recipes!

This bread turned out nice. 2 out of my 4 bananas were frozen. I thawed and drained them before adding them to be mashed up. Because of that I had to cook for an additional 25 minutes. I'll have to try this again with fresh bananas but for me I still prefer Janet's banana bread recipe on the all recipes site. It was nice having that extra cinnamon flavor though so I would still make it again just to change it up. This would make yummy muffin poppers.

Very good ..will be the go to banana bread recipe. I only had 3 bananas, can't wait to try it with 4! I also only had 2% milk so I added a dollop of Greek yogurt. Ended up turning down the temp after 60 mins.. outside was browning more quickly than the inside was setting up..reduced heat by 10 degrees and baked an additional 10min.

This recipe is fantastic! I’m so glad I followed this one. There are a lot to choose from. I subbed the butter for oil. But other than that, I followed the recipe exactly. The bread is flavorful, moist, and easy to make when you have extra bananas.
This is an awesome recipe! I added an extra egg, a half-tsp. of nutmeg, 1/4 c. sour cream, and 1/4 c. white sugar to the ingredients.
Nice!!

Great recipe. Like others, I had to bake for a little longer than the 40mins. I never tweak a recipe until I’ve made it once by the exact instructions and there’s nothing I’d change at this time about this recipe other than the bake time. I baked for 40 mins per instructions, then noticed the center was still uncooked after 40 mins. The top was a beautiful brown so I placed tin foil over the bread and baked for another 10 mins. After that extra time, the toothpick came out clean. Highly recommend. Just assess after 40 mins and alter your bake time from there.
